issues.legal_issue: A first appellate court must independently consider the facts, law, evidence, issues, and parties’ contentions and give reasoned findings, and a failure to do so warrants setting aside its judgment and remanding the appeal for fresh decision.
material_facts: The case arose from a first appeal against dismissal of a civil suit for specific performance.

The High Court dismissed the first appeal in a brief order stating that it found no justification to disturb the trial court’s findings, without addressing the grounds of appeal, the parties’ submissions, the evidence, or the issues for decision.
The appellant’s opportunity to have the first appeal decided on both facts and law was thereby adversely affected.
The Supreme Court did not decide the merits of the underlying dispute.
issues.conclusion: The appeal was allowed, the High Court’s judgment was set aside, and the first appeal was remanded to the High Court for fresh decision after hearing the parties. The High Court was directed to decide the merits uninfluenced by the Supreme Court’s observations and to give the respondent fresh notice of the hearing.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 96 read with Order 41 Rule 31 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, a first appeal is a valuable right and ordinarily reopens the whole case on fact and law. The first appellate court must address the issues and contentions pressed by the parties, consider the evidence, state its determinations and reasons, and, when reversing or varying the decree, specify the relief. A judgment that does not reflect this consideration fails to discharge the appellate court’s duty and may be set aside with the appeal remanded. The Court relied on Kurian Chacko v. Varkey Ouseph; Santosh Hazari v. Purushottam Tiwari; Madhukar v. Sangram; H.K.N. Swami v. Irshad Basith; Jagannath v. Arulappa; B.V. Nagesh v. H.V. Sreenivasa Murthy; and State Bank of India v. Emmsons International.

predicates.first_appeal_from_original_decree: A party brought a first appeal challenging a decree made after the original civil proceeding.
predicates.appellate_judgment_does_not_address_issu: The appellate court did not address the issues and the parties’ contentions that required decision.
predicates.appellate_judgment_does_not_consider_evi: The appellate court did not consider the evidence and provide reasoned findings on the matters before it.
predicates.appellant_denied_full_appellate_consider: The appellant did not receive a full consideration of the appeal on the facts and law raised.
predicates.first_appellate_judgment_set_aside_and_a: The first appellate judgment is set aside and the appeal is sent back for a fresh decision.

issues.definition: When a first appeal from an original decree is decided without addressing the issues and contentions or considering the evidence and giving reasons, and the appellant is thereby denied full appellate consideration, the first appellate judgment is set aside and the appeal is remanded for a fresh decision.
